question_bank.stem: To generate an image that shows what the classifier thinks a dog looks like, the procedure should optimize which objective?

options.text: The pre-softmax score of dog plus regularization
The post-softmax dog probability with no regularization
The validation-set accuracy after replacing dog labels
The averaged score of every animal class together

question_bank.rationale: The instructor chooses the pre-softmax dog score because it depends on the target class, and adds regularization so the optimized image does not become arbitrary noise.

distractor_rationales.B: The lecture warns that softmax can be increased by suppressing other classes, and regularization is needed.
distractor_rationales.C: Class visualization optimizes an input image, not validation accuracy after label replacement.
distractor_rationales.D: Averaging classes would not target the concept of dog.

source_ref.evidence_span: we take the pre-softmax score of dog

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows class model visualization by optimizing an input image for a chosen class score.

question_bank.stem: During class model visualization, which variable is updated by gradient ascent while the trained network is kept fixed?

options.text: The input image pixels
The class-name vocabulary
The validation labels
The training-set size

question_bank.rationale: The lecture describes forward propagating a random image, backpropagating to the pixels, and updating the pixels repeatedly.

distractor_rationales.B: The class vocabulary is not optimized in this procedure.
distractor_rationales.C: The method does not edit validation labels.
distractor_rationales.D: The data-set size is not the optimized variable.

source_ref.evidence_span: back to the pixels, and then we update the pixels

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows class model visualization by optimizing an input image for a chosen class score.

question_bank.stem: A generated Dalmatian visualization mostly shows black dots on white. What does that reveal about the classifier's learned concept?

options.text: It may associate Dalmatian with a texture cue rather than a full dog concept
It has proven that all dogs are classified by their face shape
It has converted the Dalmatian class into an occlusion mask
It has removed the need to inspect any intermediate activations

question_bank.rationale: The instructor uses the Dalmatian example to show that the model may represent the class as black dots rather than fully understanding the animal concept.

distractor_rationales.B: The example is about dot texture, not face shape for all dogs.
distractor_rationales.C: The generated image is not an occlusion mask.
distractor_rationales.D: It motivates more probing; it does not remove the need for internal inspection.

source_ref.evidence_span: it will tell you it's something with black dots

frame_evidence.description: Slide displays generated class visualizations such as Dalmatian-like black dots and grouped birds.

question_bank.stem: For activation-based data-set search, what should be collected after choosing one filter's feature map?

options.text: Validation images that produce the strongest activations in that map
Validation labels with the lowest alphabetical order
Training examples with the smallest file sizes
Random images that minimize all class scores

question_bank.rationale: The procedure is to choose a feature map, track activations on the validation set, and find the top images.

distractor_rationales.B: Alphabetical label order has no role in activation-based interpretation.
distractor_rationales.C: File size is not a proxy for a filter's learned feature.
distractor_rationales.D: The search looks for strong activations, not random minimizers.

source_ref.evidence_span: you find the top five images.

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows data-set search over top validation images or patches that maximally activate a feature map.

question_bank.stem: For a deeper feature-map activation, why does the data-set-search visualization crop a larger input region instead of a single pixel?

options.text: The deeper activation's receptive field covers a larger patch of the input
The deeper activation has no connection to the input image
The deeper activation always corresponds to a full class label
The deeper activation is computed from token embeddings

question_bank.rationale: The instructor notes that deeper activations see more of the image, so examples are cropped by tracing the activation back to its input-space receptive field.

distractor_rationales.B: The activation can be traced back to input space, which is why cropping works.
distractor_rationales.C: Intermediate activations are not necessarily full output classes.
distractor_rationales.D: Token embeddings are not part of this CNN feature-map method.

source_ref.evidence_span: the deeper the activation, the more it sees from the image.

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows data-set search over top validation images or patches that maximally activate a feature map.
